text:
Elaine: Heads-up — new regression flagged by nightly: kvcache long-context interleaved fuzz shows steady memory growth and high fragmentation after ~30m. test: synthetic_interleave_longcontext. Link: https://ci.internal/redwood/12345 :eyes:

Raj: can reproduce locally with the repro harness. run: `./tools/kv_fuzz --seed=42 --duration=1800 --sessions=64 --pattern=interleave`

Taylor: dug into perf profile. hotspots: kv_cache_eviction (44%), page_alloc_lock (18%), kv_reuse_lookup (12%). Cause seems to be repeated small allocations + no compaction path. sample perf snippet:
```
  samples  cpu  symbol
  4400     40%  kv_cache_eviction
  1800     16%  page_alloc_lock
  1200     11%  kv_reuse_lookup
```

perf-ci: nightly: synthetic_interleave_longcontext — FAILED — mem_leak > 1.2GB after 1800s (baseline 120MB). Full log attached to job 12345.

Raj: minimal repro attached in thread. Observed behavior: when sessions interleave writes at different offsets, free-list becomes highly fragmented; eviction picks pages by LRU but leaves many tiny live runs that prevent reuse; free merges rarely kick in.

Elaine: @taylor can you paste the jemalloc stats + kv allocator counters at failure point? :pray:

Taylor: jemalloc stats (trimmed):
```
active: 1.38G, allocated: 1.54G, mapped: 2.1G
narenas: 4, decay: disabled
kv_pages_created: 3420, kv_pages_evicted: 2980, kv_fragment_runs: 912
avg_run_size: 48, max_run_size: 4096
```

Javier: quick thought — kernel selection changes from last week added a single-threaded kernel path that reduces parallelism in eviction scanner. Could that interact? We switched to the new path on 1768000000.

Raj: good catch. I bisected: regression introduced between 1767998000 and 1768000500. The eviction scanner's mutex hold time increased ~2.3x after that change.

Taylor: hypothesis: longer eviction lock hold => increased concurrent small-alloc churn => fragmentation rises => reuse lookup cost explodes. Proposed mitigations:
- add a background compaction pass coalescing adjacent free runs overnight (kv_compact_worker)
- make eviction scanner more incremental (batch size limit)
- add deterministic regression test to perf-suite: synthetic_interleave_longcontext with seed matrix

Elaine: agree on test. Priority: block release if mem growth reproduces in CI. Raj, can you land the test first so we don't regress silently? :thumbsup:

Raj: I'll add the test + a lightweight guardrail in CI (fail on >300MB growth over baseline) and a bisect job. Creating PR now: https://git.internal/redwood/pulls/6789

perf-ci: new job queued: job/kv-interleave-guard — will run on dedicated pool (gpu-less) and post flakes to channel.

Javier: for quick fix we can revert single-threaded eviction path or add per-shard eviction to avoid the mutex scaling issue. Reverting is easiest to test.

Taylor: added a profiling trace snippet that shows eviction lock hold time jump after the kernel change: `evict_lock_hold_us` median 120 -> 280. Attaching flamegraph link in PR.

Raj: PR open with test + revert attempt. Running 5x in local CI now.

Elaine: if local passes, merge test-only first. Then follow up with proper compaction. Document expected behaviors in docs/kv/cache.md so QE can add coverage.

Javier: note for follow-up: also check KV cache page size policy and reuse hashmap TTL — maybe tuning those avoids compaction cost.

Taylor: thanks everyone. Filing ticket INF-2897 for longterm compaction + allocator improvements.

Elaine: :rocket: keep thread updated. If perf-ci shows green after test-land we'll schedule a canary rollback of the kernel change and run the long 6h run tomorrow.
